I've completed the unrecorded liabilities review. Summary:

**Accrued into March (US, all dated 3/31, credit 2100 Accrued Expenses — $16,380 total):**

| JE | Amount | Item | Why it's March |
|---|---|---|---|
| JE-00304 | $780 | Pinecrest Janitorial | Cleaning **performed 3/28**, invoiced 4/3 |
| JE-00305 | $3,200 | Cirrus CDN | Invoice states **service period March 2026** |
| JE-00306 | $12,400 | Whitcombe & Ames LLP | **Services rendered March 2026** |

**Deliberately excluded:** Lumen Office Leasing $14,500 — the invoice is explicitly for *April* rent, so the benefit is received in April. Paying it on 4/3 doesn't make it a March liability. I verified March rent was already correctly expensed (GL 6100 shows exactly $14,500 of March activity from invoice LUM-88858), so accruing this would have double-counted rent.

**Two judgment calls worth flagging:**

1. **JE-00306 exceeds my $10K posting authority.** I posted it as a *single* entry rather than splitting it (policy s.1 explicitly prohibits splitting to stay under the threshold) and routed it to you via `request_approval`. **It is pending your approval and blocks the close.**

2. **UK and DE could not be tested — logged as EXC-001.** All available subsequent-period evidence is US-only; there are no April invoices, payment registers, or vendor statements for UK/DE. Rather than post estimated accruals to make the entities look complete, I left them unsupported and flagged it. The auditors will ask for this, so it's worth chasing AP for the UK/DE April 1–10 payment registers now.

I also confirmed none of the four items was already in the ledger before posting, so there's no double-count. These accruals should reverse in April as the invoices hit AP. US "AP cutoff review" is marked complete; UK and DE are intentionally left open.
